ICL 2900 Series.fact: Unlike the 2980, the 2970 and the subsequent 2960 were microcoded, and thus allowed emulation of instruction sets such as that of the older 1900 Series or the System 4.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: Peripheral devices were connected using ICL's _____ (Socket/Plug and cable set) to a Port Adapter on the SMAC
ICL 2900 Series.fact: Peripheral devices were connected using ICL's Primitive Interface (Socket/Plug and cable set) to a Port Adapter on the SMAC.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: Logical addressing was employed and used a group scheme to identify system components in terms of Ports, Trunks, and _____
ICL 2900 Series.fact: Logical addressing was employed and used a group scheme to identify system components in terms of Ports, Trunks, and Streams.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: A _____ was a generic name and a hardware address within a Port to which a peripheral controller would be assigned
ICL 2900 Series.fact: Logical addressing was employed and used a group scheme to identify system components in terms of Ports, Trunks, and Streams. A Trunk was a generic name and a hardware address within a Port to which a peripheral controller would be assigned.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: A Trunk was a generic name for a controller for a number of _____ devices
ICL 2900 Series.fact: Logical addressing was employed and used a group scheme to identify system components in terms of Ports, Trunks, and Streams. A Trunk was a generic name for a controller for a number of Stream devices.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: A _____ was the generic name for the channel under which individual peripheral devices could be referenced
ICL 2900 Series.fact: Logical addressing was employed and used a group scheme to identify system components in terms of Ports, Trunks, and Streams. A Trunk was a generic name for a controller for a number of Stream devices.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: The boot process for the 2960 Series merits special mention: the OCP contained a mini _____ terminal and a cassette deck
ICL 2900 Series.fact: The boot process for the 2960 Series merits special mention: the OCP contained a mini OPER terminal and a cassette deck. The IPL code provided the means for the OCP to discover the system's hardware configuration by enquiring down the Stream(s), Trunk(s), and Port(s) to find the default or manually elected boot device for the microcode set and/or Operating System to be booted.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: At boot, the OCP would perform its _____ (IPL) from the nominated IPL device
ICL 2900 Series.fact: At boot, the OCP would perform its Initial Program Load (IPL) from the nominated IPL device.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: This process was called a GROPE or _____
ICL 2900 Series.fact: This process was called a GROPE or General Reconnaissance Of Peripheral Equipment.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: The most powerful machines, such as the _____ and 2988, implemented all instructions in hardware, whereas the others used microcoded firmware
ICL 2900 Series.fact: The most powerful machines, such as the 2980 and 2988, implemented all instructions in hardware, whereas the others used microcoded firmware.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: The 2980 allowed one or two order code processors (OCPs), each operating at up to _____ instructions per second, with real memory configurable up to 8 megabytes, with a 500-nanosecond access time
ICL 2900 Series.fact: The 2980 allowed one or two order code processors (OCPs), each operating at up to 3 million instructions per second, with real memory configurable up to 8 megabytes, with a 500-nanosecond access time.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: The _____ was initially the most powerful of ICL's New Range mainframe computers
ICL 2900 Series.fact: The 2980 allowed one or two order code processors (OCPs), each operating at up to 3 million instructions per second, with real memory configurable up to 8 megabytes, with a 500-nanosecond access time. The 2980 was initially the most powerful of ICL's New Range mainframe computers.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: Unlike the 2980, the 2970 and the subsequent 2960 were microcoded, and thus allowed emulation of instruction sets such as that of the older 1900 Series or the _____ 4
ICL 2900 Series.fact: It could run the ICL VME (VME/B, VME/K) or the Edinburgh Multiple Access System (EMAS) operating system. Unlike the 2980, the 2970 and the subsequent 2960 were microcoded, and thus allowed emulation of instruction sets such as that of the older 1900 Series or the System 4.

ICL 2900 Series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 2900 Series.question: The _____ allowed one or two order code processors (OCPs), each operating at up to 3 million instructions per second, with real memory configurable up to 8 megabytes, with a 500-nanosecond access time
ICL 2900 Series.fact: The 2980 allowed one or two order code processors (OCPs), each operating at up to 3 million instructions per second, with real memory configurable up to 8 megabytes, with a 500-nanosecond access time. The 2980 was initially the most powerful of ICL's New Range mainframe computers.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: The 7501 and 7502 systems were known as _____ in marketing publications
ICL 7500 series.fact: The 7501 and 7502 systems were called Modular Terminal Processors in marketing publications.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: 7501 and 7502 systems were built at _____, Letchworth (1/3 factory)
ICL 7500 series.fact: 7501 and 7502 systems were built at Blackhorse Road, Letchworth (1/3 factory).

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: For diagnostic purposes an _____'s Test Unit could be installed between the CPU card and the backplane
ICL 7500 series.fact: A 4 Kbyte read-only memory (ROM) in the normal address space provided a system bootstrap capable of downloading the operating software over the normal synchronous communications line, loading or dumping from/to local floppy disk or providing a local engineer's console. For diagnostic purposes an Engineer's Test Unit could be installed between the CPU card and the backplane.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: 7503 was similar to 7502 but was normally used as for _____
ICL 7500 series.fact: 7503 was similar to 7502 but was normally used as for Remote Job Entry.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: 7503 was developed by a team in _____, while 7502 was developed in Kidsgrove
ICL 7500 series.fact: 7503 was developed by a team in Stevenage, while 7502 was developed in Kidsgrove.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: Security identifiers (_____, or PID) based on magnetically-coded pens with a reader at the top right corner of the keyboard unit could be used to provide levels of access-privilege to users
ICL 7500 series.fact: Security identifiers (Personal Identity Device, or PID) based on magnetically-coded pens with a reader at the top right corner of the keyboard unit could be used to provide levels of access-privilege to users.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: Most common were the 7574 (Drico), or 7576 models but legacy devices such as the "_____" could also be attached
ICL 7500 series.fact: Most common were the 7574 (Drico), or 7576 models but legacy devices such as the "Termiprinter" could also be attached.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: In later years, more capable printers such as the _____ series became available
ICL 7500 series.fact: In later years, more capable printers such as the Okidata Microline series became available.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: This connectivity was a consequence of the 7502's implementation on the "Slow X2 _____" bus system, which was also found in the 2900 Series DCU
ICL 7500 series.fact: This connectivity was a consequence of the 7502's implementation on the "Slow X2 Highway" bus system, which was also found in the 2900 Series DCU.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: Operational software was referred to as a _____ (TE), and would vary depending upon the functions required, mainframe connection and communications protocol employed
ICL 7500 series.fact: Operational software was called a Terminal Executive (TE), and would vary depending upon the functions required, mainframe connection and communications protocol employed.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: The TEs for standard protocols and functions were written and maintained by the Kidsgrove software team, but _____ made a niche market of modifying TEs for special purposes
ICL 7500 series.fact: The TEs for standard protocols and functions were written and maintained by the Kidsgrove software team, but Letchworth Development Centre made a niche market of modifying TEs for special purposes.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: Variants for communication with IBM mainframes, X.25 networks and the _____ for Anglia Building Society and Local Government sector were examples
ICL 7500 series.fact: Variants for communication with IBM mainframes, X.25 networks and the Counter Terminal System for Anglia Building Society and Local Government sector were examples.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: The role of the _____ was essentially that of a communications front-end, and all computing functions were provided by the mainframe application
ICL 7500 series.fact: The role of the Terminal Processing Systems was essentially that of a communications front-end, and all computing functions were provided by the mainframe application.

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: However, as the trend to distributed applications developed, an end-user programming capability was introduced under the name _____ (TPL)
ICL 7500 series.fact: However, as the trend to distributed applications developed, an end-user programming capability was introduced under the name Transaction Processing Language (TPL).

ICL 7500 series.subject: Computer & IT
ICL 7500 series.question: How far these games spread is unknown, but as the TEs were single-function loading _____ would be obvious from the cessation of the normal front-end processes
ICL 7500 series.fact: The natural ingenuity of the 7500 series software developers resulted in the appearance in the early 1980s of highly specialised TEs such as Pac-Man and Space Invaders, for which the fast screen-handling abilities of the hardware was ideal. How far these games spread is unknown, but as the TEs were single-function loading Space Invaders would be obvious from the cessation of the normal front-end processes.

ICL Direct Machine Environment.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Direct Machine Environment.question: The _____ was Computing mainframe environment.
ICL Direct Machine Environment.fact: Direct Machine Environment, abbreviated DME, was a mainframe environment for microcode based versions of the ICL 2900 Series (2960 and the second-generation S-Series) of computing systems from International Computers Limited that was developed in the 1970s. DME was more-or-less an ICL 1900 order code processor in microcode, which permitted the ICL 1900 series executive, operating systems and program libraries to operate on the ICL 2900 series.

ICL Direct Machine Environment.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Direct Machine Environment.question: DME was more-or-less an ICL _____ order code processor in microcode, which permitted the ICL 1900 series executive, operating systems and program libraries to operate on the ICL 2900 series
ICL Direct Machine Environment.fact: DME was more-or-less an ICL 1900 order code processor in microcode, which permitted the ICL 1900 series executive, operating systems and program libraries to operate on the ICL 2900 series. DME was developed so that customers could buy the new hardware and run their 1900 or System 4 applications whilst they developed their replacement VME applications.

ICL Direct Machine Environment.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Direct Machine Environment.question: DME was developed so that customers could buy the new hardware and run their _____ or System 4 applications whilst they developed their replacement VME applications
ICL Direct Machine Environment.fact: DME was more-or-less an ICL 1900 order code processor in microcode, which permitted the ICL 1900 series executive, operating systems and program libraries to operate on the ICL 2900 series. DME was developed so that customers could buy the new hardware and run their 1900 or System 4 applications whilst they developed their replacement VME applications.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: The Distributed Array Processor (DAP) produced by _____ (ICL) was the world's first commercial massively parallel computer
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: The Distributed Array Processor (DAP) produced by International Computers Limited (ICL) was the world's first commercial massively parallel computer.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: The original paper study was complete in _____ and building of the prototype began in 1974
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: The original paper study was complete in 1972 and building of the prototype began in 1974.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: The first machine was delivered to Queen Mary College in _____
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: The first machine was delivered to Queen Mary College in 1979.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: Their manager and a major contributor was John K Iliffe, designer of the _____ and known for Iliffe vectors
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: Their manager and a major contributor was John K Iliffe, designer of the Basic Language Machine and known for Iliffe vectors.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: Programs for the DAP were written in _____ which was FORTRAN extended with 64×64 matrix and 64 element vector primitives
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: Programs for the DAP were written in DAP FORTRAN which was FORTRAN extended with 64×64 matrix and 64 element vector primitives. DAP Fortran compiled to an assembly language called APAL (Array Processor Assembly Language).

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: DAP Fortran compiled to an assembly language called APAL (_____)
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: DAP Fortran compiled to an assembly language called APAL (Array Processor Assembly Language).

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: The DAP had a single instruction, multiple data (_____) architecture
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: The DAP had a single instruction, multiple data (SIMD) architecture.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: The design as described in Reddaway's _____ paper is pretty much that which was implemented in the first commercial version except the facility to supply address bits from the processing elements was
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: The design as described in Reddaway's 1973 paper is pretty much that which was implemented in the first commercial version except the facility to supply address bits from the processing elements was removed.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: It was enhanced and made smaller and faster as the _____ series
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: It was enhanced and made smaller and faster as the Gamma series.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: It could be programmed in either C++ or _____-Plus
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: It could be programmed in either C++ or Fortran-Plus. These were more flexible than DAP FORTRAN, in particular they automatically took care of choosing a mapping from user specified matrix and vector bounds to the underlying hardware.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: Sample DAPs are in storage at the _____
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: Sample DAPs are in storage at the Computer History Museum.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: PERQ's broader audience than the mainframes otherwise required to utilise the DAP led ICL to estimate total sales of _____ systems by 1986 at a unit cost of £25,000
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: PERQ's broader audience than the mainframes otherwise required to utilise the DAP led ICL to estimate total sales of 1000 systems by 1986 at a unit cost of £25,000.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: Estimates of mid-_____ deliveries became dates in the first half of 1984 and then the start of 1985
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: Estimates of mid-1983 deliveries became dates in the first half of 1984 and then the start of 1985.

ICL Distributed Array Processor.subject: Computer & IT
ICL Distributed Array Processor.question: Eventually, the concept resurfaced as the DAP 510 and 610 products from the spin-off company Active Memory Technology, these arriving in _____ and 1990 respectively and providing DAP capabilities to S
ICL Distributed Array Processor.fact: Eventually, the concept resurfaced as the DAP 510 and 610 products from the spin-off company Active Memory Technology, these arriving in 1988 and 1990 respectively and providing DAP capabilities to Sun and VAX workstations.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The _____ was Range of computers.
ICL DRS.fact: The ICL DRS was a range of departmental computers from International Computers Limited (ICL).

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: Standing originally for _____, the full name was later dropped in favour of the abbreviation
ICL DRS.fact: Standing originally for Distributed Resource System, the full name was later dropped in favour of the abbreviation.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: A rebranding in late _____ pulled these together under the DRS brand, with a consistent mid-grey and peppermint-green livery
ICL DRS.fact: A rebranding in late 1988 pulled these together under the DRS brand, with a consistent mid-grey and peppermint-green livery.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The ICL division responsible for these systems eventually became part of the _____-Siemens joint venture
ICL DRS.fact: The ICL division responsible for these systems eventually became part of the Fujitsu-Siemens joint venture.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: This ran the proprietary DRX (_____) operating system
ICL DRS.fact: This ran the proprietary DRX (Distributed Resource Executive) operating system.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: It had 10 KB available for applications programs developed in _____
ICL DRS.fact: It had 10 KB available for applications programs developed in CIS COBOL.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The LAN was formed via 93 ohm coaxial cable in a bus formation running at 1.25 _____/s
ICL DRS.fact: The LAN was formed via 93 ohm coaxial cable in a bus formation running at 1.25 Mbit/s.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The final model 310 (styled like a DRS 300 module) had a second 80186 application processor with 1 MB RAM to run _____ DOS, emulating an IBM PC with a Hercules screen display
ICL DRS.fact: The final model 310 (styled like a DRS 300 module) had a second 80186 application processor with 1 MB RAM to run Concurrent DOS, emulating an IBM PC with a Hercules screen display.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: Launched in _____, DRS 300 was a modular system consisting of A4-sized units designed to be placed on an office bookshelf
ICL DRS.fact: Launched in 1986, DRS 300 was a modular system consisting of A4-sized units designed to be placed on an office bookshelf.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: Later modules used an 8 MHz processor (A2) or 80286 with 80287 maths coprocessor (A3) with up to 4 MB, and ran _____ CP/M-86 and later Concurrent DOS
ICL DRS.fact: Later modules used an 8 MHz processor (A2) or 80286 with 80287 maths coprocessor (A3) with up to 4 MB, and ran Concurrent CP/M-86 and later Concurrent DOS.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The card provided a resolution of 640 x 400 pixels with a 60 Hz refresh rate in conjunction with ICL's _____ 307 monitor
ICL DRS.fact: The card provided a resolution of 640 x 400 pixels with a 60 Hz refresh rate in conjunction with ICL's Model 307 monitor.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The initial DRS 300 also ran ICL's implementation of _____ V Release 2, DRS/NX V2, though that was never released commercially
ICL DRS.fact: The initial DRS 300 also ran ICL's implementation of Unix System V Release 2, DRS/NX V2, though that was never released commercially.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: Later an 80386 (A4) module was added, to run a 32-bit DRS/NX V3, based on System V _____ 3
ICL DRS.fact: The initial DRS 300 also ran ICL's implementation of Unix System V Release 2, DRS/NX V2, though that was never released commercially. Later an 80386 (A4) module was added, to run a 32-bit DRS/NX V3, based on System V Release 3.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The DRS 400 originated as the Clan 4, based on the _____ 68020 running UniSoft's Uniplus Unix
ICL DRS.fact: The DRS 400 originated as the Clan 4, based on the Motorola 68020 running UniSoft's Uniplus Unix. This was later replaced by the DRS 400E, based on the Motorola 68030 running DRS/NX V3.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: This was later replaced by the DRS 400E, based on the _____ 68030 running DRS/NX V3
ICL DRS.fact: The DRS 400 originated as the Clan 4, based on the Motorola 68020 running UniSoft's Uniplus Unix. This was later replaced by the DRS 400E, based on the Motorola 68030 running DRS/NX V3.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: DRS 500 originated as the _____ 5, 6 and 7 based on the CCI Power 6/32
ICL DRS.fact: The DRS 400 originated as the Clan 4, based on the Motorola 68020 running UniSoft's Uniplus Unix. DRS 500 originated as the Clan 5, 6 and 7 based on the CCI Power 6/32.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: This was built in _____ by CCI, which had been taken over by ICL's parent STC PLC
ICL DRS.fact: This was built in Irvine by CCI, which had been taken over by ICL's parent STC PLC.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: CCI was also the source of what became ICL's flagship _____Power office application suite across the DRS range
ICL DRS.fact: CCI was also the source of what became ICL's flagship OfficePower office application suite across the DRS range.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: These models largely replaced the earlier DRS 300 and DRS 400 models and were manufactured for ICL by _____
ICL DRS.fact: These models largely replaced the earlier DRS 300 and DRS 400 models and were manufactured for ICL by Acer.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The P5 Pentium-based Level 656 was launched in September _____
ICL DRS.fact: The P5 Pentium-based Level 656 was launched in September 1993.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: This product was launched in January _____ as a multiprocessor-capable SPARC-based server, running ICL's implementation of Unix System V Release 4 (SVR4)
ICL DRS.fact: This product was launched in January 1990 as a multiprocessor-capable SPARC-based server, running ICL's implementation of Unix System V Release 4 (SVR4).

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: It replaced the DRS 500 models in ICL's line-up, with two models available at launch: the _____ 40 with 25 MHz CPU and 16 MB of RAM fitted, and the Level 50 with 33 MHz CPU and 32 MB of RAM fitted
ICL DRS.fact: The P5 Pentium-based Level 656 was launched in September 1993. It replaced the DRS 500 models in ICL's line-up, with two models available at launch: the Level 40 with 25 MHz CPU and 16 MB of RAM fitted, and the Level 50 with 33 MHz CPU and 32 MB of RAM fitted.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: Input/output controllers situated on the VMEbus were also interfaced to main memory via a cache situated in the _____ linking the two buses
ICL DRS.fact: Input/output controllers situated on the VMEbus were also interfaced to main memory via a cache in the Central Services Module linking the two buses.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The HS_____ employed "hardware snoop" or "bus watching" logic to support cache coherency
ICL DRS.fact: Featuring one to four SPARC processors, up to 512 MB of RAM, 760 MB to 5 GB of storage in a single cabinet, or up to 15 GB with expansion cabinets, the DRS 6000 utilised the industry standard 32-bit VMEbus for input/output and a proprietary 64-bit HSPbus (High Speed Private bus) interfacing CPU Modules to main memory, each module providing a processor chipset and accompanying cache memory. The HSPbus employed "hardware snoop" or "bus watching" logic to support cache coherency.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: As a VMEbus controller, the _____ board employed a 68020 processor, leading to sarcastic comments in the press that it was a DRS 400 in disguise
ICL DRS.fact: As a VMEbus controller, the Central Services Module board employed a 68020 processor, leading to sarcastic comments in the press that it was a DRS 400 in disguise.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: In _____, ICL released the first multiprocessor models in the range: the DRS 6000 Level 65 and Level 70, with the latter featuring 40 MHz processors
ICL DRS.fact: In 1991, ICL released the first multiprocessor models in the range: the DRS 6000 Level 65 and Level 70, with the latter featuring 40 MHz processors.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: Some models were sold by _____ as the DS/90
ICL DRS.fact: Some models were sold by Fujitsu as the DS/90.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: ICL received the Queen's Award for Export Achievement for DRS 6000 in _____
ICL DRS.fact: ICL received the Queen's Award for Export Achievement for DRS 6000 in 1993. In 1993, ICL upgraded the DRS 6000 300 series with a 40 MHz SuperSPARC processor, introducing DRS/NX Version 7.0, an implementation of Unix System V Release 4.2.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: In _____, ICL upgraded the DRS 6000 300 series with a 40 MHz SuperSPARC processor, introducing DRS/NX Version 7.0, an implementation of Unix System V Release 4.2
ICL DRS.fact: ICL received the Queen's Award for Export Achievement for DRS 6000 in 1993. In 1993, ICL upgraded the DRS 6000 300 series with a 40 MHz SuperSPARC processor, introducing DRS/NX Version 7.0, an implementation of Unix System V Release 4.2.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: This version of DRS/NX was XPG4-compliant, supported OSF/Motif and OPEN LOOK graphical user interfaces, and promised compatibility with _____ 2 applications
ICL DRS.fact: This version of DRS/NX was XPG4-compliant, supported OSF/Motif and OPEN LOOK graphical user interfaces, and promised compatibility with Solaris 2 applications.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: It was available for both _____ and x86 platforms, marketed as a distinct product, with pricing for the latter being announced from $500.00 up to $1,600
ICL DRS.fact: In 1993, ICL upgraded the DRS 6000 300 series with a 40 MHz SuperSPARC processor, introducing DRS/NX Version 7.0, an implementation of Unix System V Release 4.2. It was available for both SPARC and x86 platforms, marketed as a distinct product, with pricing for the latter being announced from $500.00 up to $1,600.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The DRS PWS was initially released with MS-DOS 4.0 (not to be confused with the later public releases of IBM DOS 4.0 in July _____ and MS-DOS 4.01 in November 1988)
ICL DRS.fact: The DRS PWS was initially released with MS-DOS 4.0 (not to be confused with the later public releases of IBM DOS 4.0 in July 1988 and MS-DOS 4.01 in November 1988).

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: As a consequence, PWS users had a number of software compatibility challenges, although the PC Business Unit (PCBU) at _____04, in Bracknell, did patch some applications for larger customers
ICL DRS.fact: As a consequence, PWS users had a number of software compatibility challenges, although the PC Business Unit (PCBU) at ICL BRA04, in Bracknell, did patch some applications for larger customers.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The ICL/MS-DOS 4.00 _____ operating system on the ICL M60 machines has support for MS-WINDOWS 1.03
ICL DRS.fact: The ICL/MS-DOS 4.00 Multitasking operating system on the ICL M60 machines has support for MS-WINDOWS 1.03. The ICL/MS-DOS 4.10 Multitasking operating system on the ICL M60/M80 machines has support for MS-WINDOWS 1.xx and MS-WINDOWS 2.xx, including MS-WINDOWS 2.xx 286/386 in 8086 mode.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The PWS was positioned to compete with the IBM Personal System/2 (PS/2) and the DEC Vaxstation _____
ICL DRS.fact: The PWS was positioned to compete with the IBM Personal System/2 (PS/2) and the DEC Vaxstation 2000.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: In _____, the DRS PWS and DRS PWS 386 were respectively rebranded as the DRS Model 60 and DRS Model 80
ICL DRS.fact: In 1988, the DRS PWS and DRS PWS 386 were respectively rebranded as the DRS Model 60 and DRS Model 80.

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The PWS hardware was a large desktop or floor standing tower chassis, running on an _____ 8 MHz 80286 processor that was later superseded by an Intel 20 MHz 80386 (DRS PWS 386)
ICL DRS.fact: The PWS hardware was a large desktop or floor standing tower chassis, running on an Intel 8 MHz 80286 processor that was later superseded by an Intel 20 MHz 80386 (DRS PWS 386).

ICL DRS.subject: Computer & IT
ICL DRS.question: The PWS was capable of communicating with ICL departmental and mainframe services using a combination of Microlan2 and OSLAN (_____) protocols

ICL Series 39.fact: The ICL Series 39 was a range of mainframe and minicomputer computer systems released by the UK manufacturer ICL in 1985.

ICL Series 39.fact: DX System products were introduced to replace the DM1 systems, appearing in product line-ups already in late 1991.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: The _____ was Mainframe operating system by ICL.
ICL VME.fact: VME (Virtual Machine Environment) is a mainframe computer operating system developed by the UK company International Computers Limited (ICL, now part of the Fujitsu group). Originally developed in the 1970s (as VME/B, later VME 2900) to drive the then new ICL 2900 Series mainframes, it is now named OpenVME, incorporates a Unix subsystem, and runs on ICL Series 39 and Trimetra mainframe computers, and industry-standard x86-64 servers.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: VME (_____) is a mainframe computer operating system developed by the UK company International Computers Limited (ICL, now part of the Fujitsu group)
ICL VME.fact: VME (Virtual Machine Environment) is a mainframe computer operating system developed by the UK company International Computers Limited (ICL, now part of the Fujitsu group).

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: A number of influences can be seen in its design, for example _____ and ICL's earlier George 3 operating system; however it was essentially designed from scratch
ICL VME.fact: A number of influences can be seen in its design, for example Multics and ICL's earlier George 3 operating system; however it was essentially designed from scratch.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: VME/B was viewed as primarily competing with the _____/370 IBM mainframe as a commercial operating system, and adopted the EBCDIC character encoding
ICL VME.fact: A number of influences can be seen in its design, for example Multics and ICL's earlier George 3 operating system; however it was essentially designed from scratch. VME/B was viewed as primarily competing with the System/370 IBM mainframe as a commercial operating system, and adopted the EBCDIC character encoding.

There was also a project called System D, which was an advanced, highly modular operating system designed for configuring and building customized near real-time applications.

ICL VME.fact: Although it was used to bid on a system for British Rail it was subsequently cancelled because of engineering resource constraints.

ICL VME.fact: Communication between Virtual Machines is achieved by means of Events (named communication channels) and shared memory areas.

ICL VME.fact: Files and other persistent objects are recorded in a repository called the Catalogue. As well as files, the Catalogue keeps track of users and user groups, volumes, devices, network connections, and many other resources.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: As well as files, the _____ keeps track of users and user groups, volumes, devices, network connections, and many other resources
ICL VME.fact: Files and other persistent objects are recorded in a repository called the Catalogue. As well as files, the Catalogue keeps track of users and user groups, volumes, devices, network connections, and many other resources.

ICL VME.fact: It is possible to "disassemble" an SCL program from OMF back into SCL source code using the READ_SCL (or RSCL) command.

ICL VME.question: This example is taken from the _____ of implementations of Kermit

ICL VME.fact: Limited availability was then announced to existing VME customers, with others being guided towards ICL's Clan range of Unix departmental systems.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT

In 1995, ICL added support for the Internet protocol suite in the form of its UNIX Interworking Option for OpenVME, featuring implementations of TCP/IP, UDP/IP and support for the File Transfer Protocol, Telnet and Network File System (NFS) protocols.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: CADES was used in VME module development to hold separate definitions of data structures (Modes), constants (_____), procedural interfaces and the core algorithms
ICL VME.fact: CADES was used in VME module development to hold separate definitions of data structures (Modes), constants (Literals), procedural interfaces and the core algorithms.

ICL VME.question: Multiple versions ('_____') of each of these components could exist
ICL VME.fact: Multiple versions ('Lives') of each of these components could exist.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT

ICL VME.fact: The algorithms were written in System Development Language (SDL), which was then converted to S3 source by a pre-processor.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: For many years the large majority of VME users wrote applications in _____, usually making use of the IDMS database and the TPMS transaction processing monitor

ICL VME.question: Other programming languages included _____, Pascal, ALGOL 68RS, Coral 66 and RPG2, but these served minority interests
ICL VME.fact: Other programming languages included Fortran, Pascal, ALGOL 68RS, Coral 66 and RPG2, but these served minority interests.

ICL VME.question: Later, in the mid 1980s, compilers for C became available, both within and outside the _____ subsystem, largely to enable porting of software such as relational database systems
ICL VME.fact: Later, in the mid 1980s, compilers for C became available, both within and outside the Unix subsystem, largely to enable porting of software such as relational database systems.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: This is a high level language based in many ways on _____ 68, but with data types and low-level functions and operators aligned closely with the architecture of the 2900 series
ICL VME.fact: This is a high level language based in many ways on Algol 68, but with data types and low-level functions and operators aligned closely with the architecture of the 2900 series.

ICL VME.question: An assembly language SFL (_____) is also available
ICL VME.fact: An assembly language SFL (System Function Language) is also available.

ICL VME.fact: Related families of assemblers for other architectures (CALM-xx running under VME, PALM-xx developed in Pascal and running on various hosts) were developed for internal use.

ICL VME.subject: Computer & IT
ICL VME.question: Both are high-level declarative languages, using _____ as their design paradigm
ICL VME.fact: Both are high-level declarative languages, using Jackson Structured Programming as their design paradigm.

ICMPv6.question: The _____ was Internet protocol used for error messages in network operations.
ICMPv6.fact: Internet Control Message Protocol version 6 (ICMPv6) is the implementation of the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) for Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6). ICMPv6 is an integral part of IPv6 and performs error reporting and diagnostic functions.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: Secure Neighbor Discovery (_____) is an extension of NDP with extra security
ICMPv6.fact: Secure Neighbor Discovery (SEND) is an extension of NDP with extra security.

ICMPv6.fact: Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) is used by IPv6 routers for discovering multicast listeners on a directly attached link, much like Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) is used in IPv4.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: The header contains only three fields: Type (8 bits), Code (8 bits), and _____ (16 bits)
ICMPv6.fact: The header contains only three fields: Type (8 bits), Code (8 bits), and Checksum (16 bits).

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: Type: 8 bits _____ the type of the message
ICMPv6.fact: Type: 8 bits Specifies the type of the message.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: Code: 8 bits _____ field value depends on the message type and provides an additional level of message granularity
ICMPv6.fact: Code: 8 bits The Code field value depends on the message type and provides an additional level of message granularity.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: Checksum: 16 bits _____ a minimal level of integrity verification for the ICMP message
ICMPv6.fact: Code: 8 bits The Code field value depends on the message type and provides an additional level of message granularity. Checksum: 16 bits Provides a minimal level of integrity verification for the ICMP message.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: The checksum is calculated from the _____ message (starting with the Type field), prepended with an IPv6 pseudo-header
ICMPv6.fact: Checksum: 16 bits Provides a minimal level of integrity verification for the ICMP message. The checksum is calculated from the ICMP message (starting with the Type field), prepended with an IPv6 pseudo-header.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: Message body: _____ depends on the message
ICMPv6.fact: Message body: Variable Contents depends on the message.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: Some messages serve the same purpose as the correspondingly named _____ message types
ICMPv6.fact: The checksum is calculated from the ICMP message (starting with the Type field), prepended with an IPv6 pseudo-header. Some messages serve the same purpose as the correspondingly named ICMP message types.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: Note that this differs from the way it is calculated for IPv4 in _____, but is similar to the calculation done in TCP
ICMPv6.fact: Following this pseudo header, the checksum is continued with the ICMPv6 message. Note that this differs from the way it is calculated for IPv4 in ICMP, but is similar to the calculation done in TCP.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: This is followed by a _____ and destination address
ICMPv6.fact: This is followed by a Target and destination address.

ICMPv6.subject: Computer & IT
ICMPv6.question: An _____ error message must never be sent in response to another ICMP error message
ICMPv6.fact: The ICMPv6 protocol must limit the number of error messages sent to the same destination to avoid network overloading. For example, if a node continues to forward erroneous packets, ICMP will signal the error to the first packet and then do so periodically, with a fixed minimum period or with a fixed network maximum load.

Internet exchange point.fact: Internet exchange points (IXes or IXPs) are common grounds of IP networking, allowing participant Internet service providers (ISPs) to exchange data destined for their respective networks.
